ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
At 11:42 on December 20, 2015, a hillside near Baotai Garden in Fenghuang Community, Hong'ao Village, Changzhen, Guangming New District, Shenzhen, collapsed, resulting in the collapse of more than 20 factory buildings and 91 people missing. Suppose a car was parked at the bottom of a small hillside (as shown in the figure). Suddenly, the driver noticed a mudslide at a distance of $S_{1}=180\mathrm{m}$ from the bottom of the hillside, pouring down with an initial velocity of $2\mathbf{m}/\mathbf{s}$ and a uniform acceleration of $0.7\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. Assume the driver (with a reaction time of 1 second) starts the car with a uniform acceleration of $0.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ and continues to move in a uniformly accelerated straight line, while the mudslide maintains its speed upon reaching the bottom of the hillside and moves in a uniform straight line on the horizontal plane.

1. What is the velocity of the debris flow when it reaches the bottom of the slope? How long does it take to reach the bottom of the slope?
2. Starting from the moment the car begins to move, how long does it take to accelerate to the velocity of the debris flow after it reaches the bottom of the slope?
3. Can a car driver safely escape a debris flow disaster?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$16m/s$, $20s$
$32s$
The car driver can safely escape the debris flow disaster.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is a debris flow labeled Debris flow, located on a section of slope inclined downward to the right; beside the slope is labeled S1, indicating the distance from the debris flow to the bottom of the slope. The bottom of the slope is connected to a horizontal road surface, and on the horizontal road surface there is an automobile labeled Automobile; the automobile is located to the right of the bottom of the slope and escapes along the horizontal road surface. Reasoning: Take the moment when the driver just discovers the debris flow as global t=0. The debris flow undergoes uniformly accelerated motion on the slope. It is known that the initial velocity v0=2 m/s, the acceleration a=0.7 m/s^2, and the displacement S1=180 m. From v^2-v0^2=2aS1, obtain: v^2=2^2+2×0.7×180=4+252=256, so v=16 m/s. Then from v=v0+at, obtain the time to reach the bottom of the slope: t=(16-2)/0.7=20 s. The automobile has a 1 s reaction time, therefore it begins to move only from global t=1 s. The automobile starts from rest and accelerates uniformly with a_car=0.5 m/s^2, and the automobile speed v_car=0.5t, where t here is the time counted from when the automobile starts to move. Let v_car=16 m/s, obtain 0.5t=16, so t=32 s. Safety comparison: The global moment when the automobile speed reaches 16 m/s is 1+32=33 s. At this time, the distance traveled by the automobile after starting is s_car=(1/2)×0.5×32^2=256 m. The debris flow reaches the bottom of the slope at global t=20 s, and afterward moves uniformly on the horizontal plane at 16 m/s. By global t=33 s, the horizontal motion time is 33-20=13 s, and the horizontal displacement is s_mud=16×13=208 m. At this time the automobile is ahead of the debris flow by 256-208=48 m; and afterward the automobile speed continues to increase, exceeding the debris flow speed, therefore it will not be caught up with.
